summary: Describes IANA actions to take over registries for the Licklider Transmission Protocol, Compressed Bundle Header Encoding and Bundle Protocol, previously ad hoc registries of the DTNRG. This is administrative work rather than a new protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: Research friends handed their sign-up lists to an official librarian.

questions: ltp cbhe bundle protocol iana registries
how are delay-tolerant network protocols registered
subtitle: Moving experimental protocol registries under official IANA management.

tldr.problem: The DTNRG research group created ad hoc registries for experimental delay-tolerant networking protocols (LTP, CBHE, Bundle Protocol), but as these specifications matured and gained multiple interoperable implementations, the registries needed official management.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC requests that IANA formally take over management of the registries for Licklider Transmission Protocol (LTP), Compressed Bundle Header Encoding (CBHE), and Bundle Protocol, establishing registration policies and initial values. Some ranges are delegated to CCSDS SANA for space missions.
tldr.outcome: Stable, officially managed registries for delay-tolerant networking protocols, with clear policies for how new values are assigned, and coordination with space agencies through the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems.

today: RFC 7116 was updated by RFC 9758. IANA continues to maintain these registries, and the registries are actively used by delay-tolerant networking systems, including those deployed in extreme environments and space missions.

sections.title: Moving Registries to IANA
sections.content:
The Delay-Tolerant Networking Research Group (DTNRG) defined three related protocols for communication in challenged environments: Licklider Transmission Protocol (LTP) [RFC5326], Compressed Bundle Header Encoding (CBHE) [RFC6260], and the Bundle Protocol [RFC5050]. These protocols contain fields with assigned numeric values that require registries to track.

During the research phase, the group maintained ad hoc registries for these values. As the specifications stabilized and gained multiple interoperable implementations, the group determined that these registries should be handed off to IANA for official, long-term management. This RFC describes the registries IANA has created, the registration policies that govern them, and the initial values for each registry.
sections.plainLanguage: When researchers are experimenting, they keep notes in a notebook. Once things work and people are using it, they hand the notebook to an official office that keeps it safe and organized.

sections.title: LTP Registries
sections.content:
The Licklider Transmission Protocol defines three fields requiring registries. The first is Cancel Segment Reason Codes: when LTP cancels a data transfer, it includes a reason code. Values 0 through 5 are defined in RFC 5326 (client service canceled, unreachable service, retransmission limit exceeded, miscolored data, system error, and retransmission limit again). Values 6 through 255 are available for assignment using the Specification Required policy.

Second, LTP Engine IDs identify LTP service instances. The ID space is divided into ranges: 1 through 2^14-1 require Expert Review; 2^14 through 2^21-1 are allocated to CCSDS (space missions); 2^21 through 2^28-1 are private or experimental; 2^28 through 2^42-1 are available on a First Come First Served basis. Third, LTP Client Service IDs identify services using LTP (such as the Bundle Protocol, value 1, or LTP Service Data Aggregation, value 2). Ranges 4 through 2^14-1 are allocated to CCSDS, 2^14 through 32767 are private or experimental, and 32768 and above require specification.
sections.plainLanguage: LTP has three lists: why transfers are canceled, who the LTP engines are, and what services are talking over LTP. Each list has reserved slots for official things, space stuff, experiments, and anyone who asks.

sections.title: CBHE and Bundle Protocol Registries
sections.content:
The Compressed Bundle Header Encoding specification requires two registries. CBHE Node Numbers identify network nodes in the 'ipn' URI scheme. Like LTP Engine IDs, the value space is segmented: 1 through 2^14-1 for Expert Review; 2^14 through 2^21-1 for CCSDS; 2^21 through 2^28-1 for private or experimental use; 2^28 through 2^42-1 for first-come-first-served; and 2^42 and above reserved. CBHE Service Numbers identify service types (Bundle Protocol Administrative Records, value 0; CCSDS File Delivery Service, value 1). Values 0-63 require specification; 64-1023 are allocated to CCSDS; 1024 to 2^16-1 require specification; 2^16 and above are private or experimental.

The Bundle Protocol itself defines Administrative Record Types, a 4-bit field. Values 0 is reserved, 1 is bundle status report, 2 is custody signal (all from RFC 5050), and 3-15 are unassigned and available via Specification Required.
sections.plainLanguage: CBHE needs two lists: which network nodes exist, and what services can run on them. Bundle Protocol adds a list of administrative message types. All three use a similar pattern: some are official, some are for space, some are free to claim.

sections.title: Space Mission Delegation
sections.content:
A significant portion of the registry value spaces are delegated to the CCSDS Space Assigned Numbers Authority (SANA). CCSDS is the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems, and SANA maintains registries for protocols used by its member agencies (space agencies and space organizations worldwide).

Delegating ranges to SANA recognizes that space communication is a specialized domain with different requirements. Missions often coordinate in advance, and having a dedicated authority for space-related values allows IANA to focus on terrestrial and general-purpose uses while SANA manages the space mission namespace. This document specifies the ranges handed to SANA for each registry, typically the mid-tier ranges that allow both official assignments and research use.
sections.plainLanguage: Space missions are special and coordinate together through CCSDS, so they get their own section of each list. IANA and SANA work together so neither one has to do the other's job.
